title: Summer and Orchard
premise: Ines Montrose built her wedding-planning empire on the ruins of her own failed marriage, and she has no intention of believing in love again — until a probate error names her, alongside her estranged first love Theo Calloway, as co-owner of the stubborn Bramble Hollow orchard where they grew up. Forced to share the land for one summer while the deed is untangled, Ines and Theo clash over its future: she sees a lucrative venue that could save her floundering company, he sees the working orchard his late grandmother swore to protect. As their old feelings reignite and a rival planner schemes to seize both the orchard and Ines's clients, Ines must choose between the career that saved her and the truth about why she left Theo in the first place. She chooses truth, testifies against her own company's fraudulent lease bid, and stays through harvest — choosing Theo, the orchard, and a second chance with honest timing at last.
about_author: Mara Vane is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade planning other people's perfect days before turning to fiction. She writes romances about people who are very good at organizing everyone's life but their own.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On the worst week of her career — a botched society wedding and a sinking company — a lawyer delivers news: she co-owns Bramble Hollow orchard with a name she hasn't spoken in twelve years. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into dread as the past arrives by certified mail.

chapters.title: Cider and Grudges
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo returns to the dying orchard he abandoned after his grandmother's funeral, determined to sell nothing and fix everything alone — until Ines walks up the gravel drive in city shoes. Emotional beat: resentment sharpened by unwanted tenderness; neither will be the first to leave.

chapters.title: Terms of Occupation
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They negotiate an uneasy truce: split the property line down the middle of the oldest apple row until probate resolves. Ines secretly scouts the orchard as a wedding venue to save her company. Emotional beat: guarded cooperation laced with flirtation each pretends not to notice.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Clearing the farmhouse attic, Theo finds his grandmother's letters revealing she once refused a developer's fortune to keep the orchard whole — and a letter addressed to Ines, never sent. Emotional beat: grief softening into understanding of what loyalty actually costs.

chapters.title: Rain on the Packing Shed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A storm traps them overnight repairing the packing shed roof; soaked and laughing, they nearly kiss before Ines pulls back, terrified. Flashback reveals she left Theo twelve years ago because his family blamed her for the fire that nearly destroyed the orchard. Emotional beat: longing colliding with buried guilt.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sleek planner Vivienne Marsh arrives claiming Ines's company already optioned the orchard for development, showing Theo a signed-looking term sheet. Feeling betrayed, Theo signs with Vivienne's buyer instead. Emotional beat: betrayal rekindling every old wound; loyalty tested by plausible lies.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers Vivienne forged her signature and plans to raze the orchard — and that her own business partner authorized it to save the firm. Confronting him costs her the company she built. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into clarity; she finally chooses truth over survival.

chapters.title: The Hearing Under the Old Row
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the probate hearing, Ines testifies against the fraudulent bid, exposing Vivienne and surrendering her career's last lifeline. Theo, moved, withdraws his sale agreement. The judge orders mediation: one season to decide the orchard's fate together. Emotional beat: public reckoning; two people stripped to honesty.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Working the harvest side by side, they read the unsent letter aloud — his grandmother forgave Ines years ago and begged Theo not to let pride cost him what the fire didn't. Theo asks Ines to stay, not as co-owner but as himself asking her. Emotional beat: forgiveness landing like ripened fruit finally falling.

chapters.title: Summer, Again
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. One year later: the orchard thrives as a small, honest events space run on their terms, hosting weddings Ines can finally believe in. The epilogue scene is their own quiet ceremony under the oldest apple row, no planners, just neighbors and cider. Emotional beat: belonging earned; second chances kept with better timing.
